To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a polymorphism in the gene encoding activin-like kinase 1, a protein that is mutated in a familial brain arteriovenious malformation (BAVM) syndrome, is associated with BAVMs in a large cohort of patients with sporadic BVMs.
the ALK1 IV3-35A> G polymorphism is associated with sporatic brain arteriovenious malformation.
a genetic variant in a protein known to play a role in hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia is associated with sporatic brain arteriovenos malformations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling pathway in the pathogenesis of sporadic and familial brain arteriovenus malformations (bAVM).
the genetic basis for sporadic brain arteriovenous malformations,
the role of genetic factors in the development of sporadic brain arteriovemous malformations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a common polymorphism in the ALK1 gene is associated with sporadically occurring BAVMs.
the ALK1 IV3-35A > G polymorphism was associated in a case control analysis of sporadic BAVMS.
genetic variation in ALK1 may contribute to sporadic BAVMS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ALK1 IVSS3-35G allele is a risk factor for sporadic BAVs, and that the ENG -1742G, ENG -207A and ALK1 IV5S3-35G alleles may also be risk factors.
genetic variation in TGF-beta signaling genes is associated with sporatic BAVM.

the ALK1 IVSS-35A>G is significantly associated with sporadic BRAVMs, and the ENG -1742G>A and ENG 207A>G polymorphisms are associated with sporadis BRAVMs, although this association did not reach statistical significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are genetic variants associated with sporadic arteriovenous fistulas that may be important in the development of these lesions and that may be important to consider in the future when treating these lesions.

there is a strong genetic component to brain arteriovenus malformations, and this is the first evidence that genetic variations in the same genes that cause hereditary hemorrhage telangiectasia may also contribute to sporadic brain arterovenous malformation.
there is a common polymorphism in the gene ALK1 (which encodes a receptor for the TGF-beta protein) that is strongly associated with the presence of brain arteriovenus malformation.
